raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou for more than half a century. My father farmed before me, and I learned by watching and doing. I don't read extension pamphlets. I do what has worked, what my neighbors do, and what my body can still manage at 70 — I live alone now, so I have to be realistic about how much work I can take on.

My 10.1 mu splits into two parts in my head: about 7 mu of my flat, good ground runs wheat in winter then maize right after harvest — same plot, back to back, like always. The other 3.1 mu I keep in cotton. I've thought about dropping the cotton because it wears me out, but it brings cash when prices are decent, so I'll keep it a bit smaller this year and manage it carefully.

**Wheat:** I'll plant in October, after I rotary-till the field following maize harvest. I use the same improved variety I've bought from the village co-op for the last several years — not hybrid, just a reliable semi-dwarf. I'll put down compound fertilizer at sowing, then come back with urea at jointing. I'll irrigate three times: once at sowing to get a good stand, once at jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide sprays — one for disease around heading, one if I see aphids. Expecting around 450 jin per mu, maybe a bit more if spring rains cooperate.

**Maize:** Right after I cut the wheat in June, I seed the maize directly into the stubble — no time for tillage in summer, the rains are coming and the season is short. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, same as most people around here. I apply more nitrogen for maize — it's hungry. Two irrigations if summer rain is thin, maybe just one if it's a wet year. Two pesticide passes. Should yield around 550 jin per mu.

**Cotton:** I plough this plot in spring, plant in late April. I use the hybrid Bt cotton seed — it saves me some pest work, though I still need to spray. Cotton needs a lot of attention I can't always give. I'll water four times — it's thirsty in the flowering and boll-setting stage. Six pesticide applications is what I usually end up doing. I expect maybe 250 jin of seed cotton per mu if the summer is not too hot and dry.
